title: The great circle: the Kav's first will, like a man's taste and his dream house
overview:
The *Kav* goes down in circles (*igulim*) and in a straight line (*yosher*) shaped like a person, and its first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, surrounds all four worlds equally. To explain it the chapter sets out two kinds of will. The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, yet it is hidden, part of his self-knowledge, with no general and particular. Only when he comes to build does it become a composite will: one general picture of the house, then the kitchen, the sink, down to the *mezuza* on the door.

Above, *tehiru ila'a* is G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way. After the *tzimtzum* comes the choice: this world, all the way to *Moshiach*, as one *ratzon kadum* that includes every detail, even each hair and each leaf in the wind. Everything after it, *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, down to the weather today, is only a means to that goal. That a will can be cut off from its goal is the root of *Tohu*.

terms.gloss: circles: the ten concentric circles the Kav makes as it goes down, like the soul before it comes into the body
the straight line: the sefiros in the form of a person, three lines, like the soul in the body with each power in its own kli
the lower purity: the first circle after the hiyuli Kav, the ultimate goal; self-knowledge of how something separate relates to Him
the raw potential from which all the particular drawings-down branch off
the simple will in the Essence, still one with it; it cannot yet be called a general thought
the absolute will: like a person's taste or style, which shapes every choice and stays hidden
the composite will: a will for something in the world, with a general thing, details and priorities
self-knowledge: knowing what you will want because you know yourself
the upper purity: before the tzimtzum, only G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way
the original will: the ultimate goal, of which everything after it is only a detail and a means
the encompassing light; the first circle surrounds all four worlds equally

sections.title: Circles and the straight line: the first circle is tehiru tata'a
sections.summary: The chapter now explains the *makifim* and *pnimiyim* in the *Kav*: the ten circles (*igulim*) it makes as it goes down, and the straight line (*yosher*) in the form of a person. The first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, is *tehiru tata'a*, the general *makif* over all four worlds equally: the ultimate goal of the whole chain.

phrases.he: (טז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו וחוט זה, איך שיש בו בחינת מקיפים ופנימיים
phrases.en: Now we're going to explain the *inyan* of *igulim v'yosher*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים מתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו' (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)

blocks.text:
Chapter 16 is "a nice *perek*": pretty short and quick and simple, one pretty simple *inyan*, and most people find it very *geshmak* (tasty); "it sits very well."

**Now we're going to explain the inyan of igulim v'yosher**: the circles (*igulim*) and the straight line (*yosher*) that are the *makifim* and the *pnimiyim* of the *Kav*.

As it says in *Etz Chaim*, it "circles and returns and circles." First the *hiyuli Kav* goes down a little bit, then it makes a circle; then it goes down a little more and makes another circle, and so on until it makes ten. Those are the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon*. Then comes *yosher*.

The truth is that the *igulim* and *yosher* are really two separate *hishtalshelus*'s (chains of descent): every single world has ten *sefiros* of *igulim* and ten *sefiros* of *yosher*.

blocks.question: Is it like a spring?
blocks.text: No. It is as if you drew a bunch of concentric circles and had a line going through them. It is not spiraling down. Each one is a full circle that closes; then from the same line it goes down again and makes the next one. It is like a *Kav* coming from one side, going down and making all the circles.

blocks.title: Water filling carved troughs
blocks.text:
From the side of the *reshimu*, the circles are set up from below to above, and they are not connected at all. But when the *yosher* comes down, the *Kav* starts from the top, and in the light they are connected.

It is as if a trough was engraved in the shape of a circle, and water was coming down. It comes down from the top, hits the first trough, fills it up, overflows to the next one and goes around that. What makes the light stop in each place and circle? The *reshimu* has already carved out an *igul* there. From the *reshimu* there is no line connecting them, only concentric circles; then the *Kav* comes down from the top, hits a circle, goes around it, and after it fills it goes down again. And it does not fill the whole inside: it just goes around the rim, so to speak. You could make it like a bead thing, with a marble. "That's like the way the *mashal* of it." That line is the *yosher* of the *igulim*.

These are the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* as they are in the light. *Yosher* comes after them, and at the same time there is a parallel *hishtalshelus* on top of it: the *sefiros* of *yosher*, in the shape of a person, the three lines of *Chabad*, *Chagas*, *Nehi*, with *chachma* on the right and *bina* on the left. That whole form of an *adam* (a man) is the *yosher*.

The two chains overlap. The *igulim* start a little higher; from about the *bina* of the *igulim* it connects right to *yosher*, and the rest of the *igulim* overlap with *yosher*, in the same place.

blocks.title: The soul before and in the body
blocks.text:
The *igulim* are like the soul before it comes into the body; *yosher* is the way it goes into the body, where each part of the soul gets its own *kli* (vessel) and becomes a *partzuf*. In the soul all the powers are like one, and you cannot really tell one from the other: the power of will and the power of walking are like the same thing, because when it wants something, it is already drawn towards it. It is all spiritual, so all ten happen together. In the body each power becomes distinct, because it is tied to its own *kli*, and that lets you appreciate each one: that makes a *partzuf*.

The Mitteler Rebbe's *mashal*, in this chapter and the next three, will make clear what *igulim* and *yosher* mean, as is explained elsewhere at length.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף ועיגול הראשון
phrases.en: in the first circle, right after the *hiyuli Kav*, there's the first circle.

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה כו',
phrases.en: That's called the lower purity.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת המקיף הכללי שמקיף לד' עולמות דאבי''ע בשווה
phrases.en: This is the general *makif* that surrounds the four worlds of *ABYA* equally.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text:
**In the first circle, right after the hiyuli Kav, there's the first circle**, and it is called *tehiru tata'a*: **the lower purity**. It is the first will, the first *gilui* (revelation) after the *tzimtzum*, an actual revelation of the will for the *hishtalshelus*: the general *makif*, *sovev kol almin*, after the *tzimtzum*. It is the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* as it is after the *tzimtzum*.

It is the first thing that came out from the *hiyuli Kav*. First is the *reshis hakav* (the beginning of the line), learned in the last three chapters: the short line, the *kav hamida* (line of measure). But that, as was said, is only a *hiyuli* for the particular revelations.

blocks.title: The teacher's ultimate goal
blocks.text: Once the teacher has figured out his system, how to divide up the subject into levels to measure the student, he makes his first circle: the ultimate goal of this will, of this whole *hishtalshelus*.

blocks.title: Rabbi Chodakov and the shliach to South Africa
blocks.text:
This is like the unrealistic goal in the story of Rabbi Chodakov told at the *farbrengen* ("I told you this story?"). A *shliach* (emissary) was going to South Africa, and Rabbi Chodakov asked him, "Do you have a plan for what you're planning to do there?" He said, "No, when I get there, I'll see."

The idea of that story is that your goal first has to be your pure, unrealistic goal. What do you want, essentially? Then you figure out how to make it fit in.

So this first circle is what the teacher figures out first: "What would be the ultimate thing, if I could get the students to come out from this class? What do I want them to come out with?" It is the all-encompassing desire that includes any scenario that will happen in this classroom, in this *hishtalshelus*, because it is the best you could get within it.

**This is the general makif that surrounds the four worlds of ABYA equally.** This is what is usually called *sovev kol almin*. Sometimes the light before the *tzimtzum* is also called *sovev kol almin*, but that is different, because it is not a *sovev* on a *pnimi*, as was said before and will be explained now. **Like it says in Etz Chaim.**

sections.title: The Kav as one general thought that sees to the end
sections.summary: First the *Kav* as a whole: one *hiyuli* from which all the particular drawings-down branch off. It is like a general thought that sees to the end of all generations at a glance, as a man who wants a house already wants the kitchen, the sink and the running water.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים
phrases.en: but first we have to explain,

phrases.he: כללות ענין הקו הזה, איך שהוא בחינת היולי כללי לכל הסתעפות המשכות פרטיים הרבה שמסתעפים ממנו עד סוף העשיה כו' כנזכר לעיל
ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע בענין מחשבה כללית
שבמחשבה זו הכללית צופה ומביט עד סוף כל הדורות בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that with this general thought Hashem sees the whole *hishtalshelus*, with the whole history of mankind, all the way to the end,

phrases.he: (ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו מה שבידיעת עצמו יודע את כל הנבראים
phrases.en: This is what the *Rambam* describes, that by knowing Himself He knows all the *nivra'im*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: **But first we have to explain** the *Kav* as a whole: how it is one general *hiyuli* for all the many particular drawings-down that branch off from it, down to the end of *Asiya*. *Mistaef* means to branch off, "whatever *lashon* it is."

It is understood from the known *mashal* of a general thought: **with this general thought Hashem sees the whole hishtalshelus, with the whole history of mankind, all the way to the end**, to the end of the seventh millennium, the total completion, even past *Moshiach*. *Moshiach* is the end of the sixth millennium; after it, in the seventh, is "all this stuff that we're going to do then, whatever that is." This is what is called the *ratzon kadum* or the *machshava kduma*.

In the Rambam's words: **by knowing Himself He knows all the nivra'im** (the created beings).

blocks.title: Do you want a sink in your kitchen?
blocks.text:
How can one thought include everything you want to come out? Like a guy who wants a house. You ask him, "Do you want a kitchen in your house?" "Yeah, what do you mean? Of course. I said I want a house. What kind of a house would it be without a kitchen?" "Okay, so you want a kitchen. Do you want a sink in your kitchen?" "What do you mean? If I said I want a kitchen, what kind of a kitchen would it be without the sink?" "Okay, okay, so you want a sink. Do you want running water in your sink?"

You could go through the whole house like this. The word "house" is one thought that includes all the details, even ones less obvious than that, because he wants *his* house. Since he knows himself, what he likes, he knows what he wants in his house.

blocks.title: 126,282 hairs on his head
blocks.text: So if G-d said He wants a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), you ask Him, "Do you want this and this guy in your *dira b'tachtonim*?" He says, "What do you mean? How can I have a *dira b'tachtonim* without this guy?" And even if you get down to "Do you want him to have 126,282 hairs on his head?": "He wouldn't be Moishe without that, you know?" All the details are included like this.

sections.title: Two kinds of will: the simple will is a person's taste, the composite will has priorities
sections.summary: The simple will in the Essence is like a person's taste or style: it already shapes how he will do every kindness and think every thought, but it is hidden and has no general and particular. Only when it comes to action does it become a composite will (*ratzon murkav*): a general thought with particulars under it, circle within circle.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע
שיש ב' מיני רצון
phrases.en: There's two types of desires.

phrases.he: א' רצון הפשוט שבעצמות
phrases.en: One is the simple *ratzon* that's in the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: שנכלל בעצמותו ממש,
שלא נקרא עדיין בשם בחינת מחשבה ורצון כללי
phrases.en: You can't call it a general thought or general *ratzon* yet,

phrases.he: כי מתאחד עדיין בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: still one with his *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: כמו גם שהוחלט רצון זה כבר בעצמו
phrases.en: even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak,

phrases.he: איך לעשות דבר חסד פלוני
או איך לדבר ולחשוב אותו
phrases.en: or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think.

phrases.he: או להשכיל שכל פרטי
phrases.en: or also the way that each person understands things in different ways.

phrases.he: או להיות לו רצון ותענוג בדבר כו'
phrases.en: or whether he's going to enjoy something or not enjoy something,

blocks.text: **There's two types of desires.** **One is the simple ratzon that's in the Atzmus**, the *ratzon hapashut*, included in His very essence. **You can't call it a general thought or general ratzon yet**, because it is **still one with his Atzmus**.

It includes **even the way that he has already predetermined in himself, so to speak**, how to do a particular kindness. In other words, his taste: the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will) is like his taste or his style, already in his essence. It is not an actual desire or an actual thought of the outside world. It is part of his self-knowledge: he has a certain sense of who he is and how he wants to express himself. That is what he made like *Kadmon*: a certain estimation of how he wants to reveal himself.

So he already knows how he will want to do a particular kindness: if such a situation comes up, he knows he is going to want to give the guy the coat, and he is going to do it. Each person has his way. If you know a person really well, you can predict how they will do something. This is the level of *Kadmon* spoken of before: the *ratzon hamuchlat* is *Kadmon*.

As was said before, it is from *Kadmon* that a little of it actually comes out, but it will not come out *b'pnimiyus* (inwardly), as will be explained now, because a person's taste is not yet a desire for any particular thing. It relates to everything he does: it is the aspect of him that relates to what he does. How he wants to do it, **or what he's going to say, and what he's going to think**: even what he thinks includes his biases, so that if a certain situation comes up, different people will think about it in a certain way.

**Or also the way that each person understands things in different ways**: each one will understand a certain *sechel* (idea) in a certain way. As will be said later, everybody, Rashi, Tosafos, each person has a certain *shita* (approach), a way of understanding things that is unique. **Or whether he's going to enjoy something or not enjoy something**, what he is going to like and what he is going to hate: all these are included in his taste. "That's basically what I would call this."

phrases.he: הגם שמתחבר רצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון בדבר הפרטי
phrases.en: even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it,

phrases.he: אבל נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: but it stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן אין בו עדיין בחינת כלל ופרט כו'
phrases.en: and that therefore their taste does not have a *klal u'prat*.

blocks.text: **Even though this taste connects to the actual desire, it influences it, but it stays really hidden.**

blocks.title: The artist's style
blocks.text: Take an artist with a certain style. The style is not something tangible. When he makes a painting, it is influenced by his style, but you cannot say that the painting is his style. You cannot directly copy it or say what it is; you could not really try to do it. Sometimes people do try to figure out what their style is and do those things, and it comes out fake.

A style means that you are just being yourself, and it is natural. In books on writing, or on any type of art, they say it nicely: the style is the person himself. *Davka* (precisely) when you are not trying, when you just let yourself come out freely without putting anything on, not even acting the way you see yourself, it comes out in everything you do. But it is nothing particular that you could point to: you can say a painting is impressionistic, but you cannot say it is impressionism.

The same way, a person's taste influences every desire he ever has, but no desire is a direct expression of his full taste.

**And that therefore their taste does not have a klal u'prat** (general and particular). When a person wants a house, the main thing he wants is the building with a roof, to be protected from the elements. The secondary things are the furniture and the utilities; then he is going to decorate it, paint it, put down carpeting or a wood floor, and then there are the bathroom drapes.

It is all influenced by his taste. But when it comes out in an actual will, there is the main thing: the first will, the main circle, is for a house, a general picture of what a house means. Within that there is a circle for the kitchen, a circle for the living room and the dining room and the bedroom and the bathroom, each with its own circle included in the general circle of the house. Each of those has circles in it, like the sink and the stove in the kitchen, smaller and smaller circles for each detail that was included in the general thought, down to the smallest details like the bathroom drapes.

But the taste influences each stage equally. Whenever there is a choice to be made of how to do it, big or small, that choice comes from his taste, his *ratzon hamuchlat*. And since his *ratzon hamuchlat* is involved, each one is an expression of it just like anything else.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זה עולה רצון זה שהוחלט אצלו לבוא לידי מעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: but when this *ratzon* is going to come now *b'poel mamash*,

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מהעלמו לגלוי
phrases.en: when it comes *b'poel mamash*, actually do it, then it becomes revealed, *l'gilui*,

phrases.he: אז יבוא הרצון בבחינת כלל ופרט,
phrases.en: then there's a general thing and there's the particulars,

phrases.he: דהיינו מחשבה כללית
phrases.en: first there's the general thought

phrases.he: שכוללת כל ענין המעשה מראש לסוף בסקירה א'
phrases.en: that includes everything at once,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצונות פרטיים
phrases.en: then it divides to particular desires,

phrases.he: ולכל רצון שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and each one has its own *sechel* and *middos* and everything,

phrases.he: ובאין זה אחר זה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: and they come one after the other,

phrases.he: זה עליון מקיף לתחתון,
phrases.en: the upper one encompassing the lower one,

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך האופן כו'
phrases.en: like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא רצון המורכב שיש בו כלל ופרט
phrases.en: that's called a *ratzon murkav*, a complex *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **But when this ratzon is going to come now b'poel mamash** (into actual deed): if you know somebody very well, you could figure out his dream house even before he ever thought of buying a house. But there you cannot say there is a general and a particular, because there is no deed there at all. He did not even think about it.

That is also how you recognize that his taste would come out in the society we are in now. The same person living in a different time would express the same taste in a different way: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa.

sensitivity.reason: Illustrates another time and place with "a hut if he were a tribal chief in Africa"; not meant as disparaging, but a stereotype of Africa a public edition may prefer to drop.
sensitivity.publishable: That is also how you recognize that his taste would come out in the society we are in now. The same person living in a different time would express the same taste in a different way: instead of a nice, big mansion, he would want whatever house fit a leader of that time and place.

blocks.text: **When it comes b'poel mamash, actually do it, then it becomes revealed**, and **then there's a general thing and there's the particulars**: there are priorities. **First there's the general thought that includes everything at once**, that defines everything: what is the general goal here. **Then it divides to particular desires, and each one has its own sechel and middos** (intellect and emotions). **And they come one after the other** in a chain, **the upper one encompassing the lower one**: it defines and includes the lower one, and the lower one is just the detail to serve that general purpose, **like a circle inside of a circle, concentric circles.**

When you actually have a will for a house, a general will for the house, and a particular will for the kitchen, and the will for the kitchen has the particular wills for the sink and all these things, **that's called a ratzon murkav, a complex ratzon**. *Murkav* means composite, made of many parts. That is the whole will for the house when it comes *b'poel mamash*, as opposed to the taste. The taste is a simple will, *ratzon pashut*. When you actually want something in the world it is complex: the general thing has many details, each with sub-details, so there is already a *klal* and a *prat*.

*Murkav* also means that there are priorities. A simple thing from the essence is just a *nekuda* (a point). Here it is complicated, because you can have conflicting desires: you want this, you want that, you want this because it will do that, "it's like a whole bubble already." The choice in each will comes from the *ratzon pashut*, from his *ratzon hamuchlat*; the actual picture of it, the way it comes out physically, is *murkav*.

As will be said soon, maybe at the beginning of the next chapter, the *ratzon hamuchlat* is really for himself: it is a self-expression. He is comfortable *davka* in a certain way, he wants to express a certain atmosphere, and the house he wants expresses him. As far as that goes, the *ratzon hamuchlat* is really just a will to express himself. ("That's already *muchlat*, yeah. *Murkav*, right," he answers someone in the room.)

sections.title: The mashal: a man who wants to build a great building
sections.summary: The taste a man already has for a building is still within himself, as if it did not exist; the house is not yet wanted. When he comes to build, the details he had already settled appear, first as one general picture, then will after will down to the last screw and the *mezuza* on the door.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע,
אדם שרוצה לבנות בנין גדול
phrases.en: a person wants to build a big building,

phrases.he: כפי הרצון שהוחלת מכבר אצלו
phrases.en: according to his taste,

phrases.he: להיות בו אופנים מיוחדים דוקא
phrases.en: he wants it to be specially designed for the way he wants it.

phrases.he: שאותו הרצון שהוחלט אצלו מכבר,
phrases.en: that this taste that he had already decided before,

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בא במדה ותענוג מיוחד
phrases.en: even though in a way it is like defined, that each person has a certain thing, they enjoy things in a certain way,

phrases.he: באופן כך וכך,
וממילא בשכל ומדות בא בשיעור ומדה כו',
phrases.en: and since he enjoys things a certain way, that automatically influences that his *sechel* leans to try to find that; everything is in line with that.

phrases.he: אך כל זה הוא השיעור וההחלט שבעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: that's all still within his essence,

phrases.he: ונכלל בעצמו
phrases.en: and it's really part of himself,

phrases.he: והיה כלא היה כו'
phrases.en: it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.

blocks.text: It is understood from a known *mashal*: **a person wants to build a big building, according to his taste**; **he wants it to be specially designed for the way he wants it.** He wants to build a dream house, or a dream facility for his Chabad house; it does not make a difference what it is.

**This taste that he had already decided before**, **even though in a way it is like defined, that each person has a certain thing, they enjoy things in a certain way**, **and since he enjoys things a certain way, that automatically influences that his sechel leans to try to find that; everything is in line with that.** But **that's all still within his essence, and it's really part of himself**: **it's like it doesn't exist; he doesn't actually have a desire yet for a house.**

If you know him, you would know how he would want it, but he does not actually have a desire for it, and there is no actual thought of anything outside himself yet. It is *yedias atzmo* (self-knowledge). How do you know what you want when you are planning a house, even before you thought about it? You think what makes you happy, and that lets you know what you want, because you know how you want to feel. The *pnimiyus* (inner side) of it is the way you want to feel, and that you like to do things a certain way.

That comes because he set up a certain thing in his personality *b'kadmonius*, a certain *teva* (nature), so to speak, for himself. That personality is the form he chose to express himself with, and it comes out in the world according to whatever situation it comes out in.

That is the *inyan* of *teshuva* (return): you reconnect the external desires to their source, and the farther up you go, the more it is like hitting the reset button. The higher up you change a desire, the more flexible it makes everything under it. If you go all the way up to the essence, everything becomes flexible, because the whole point there is to express that you have *bechira* (free choice), that you are not bound by anything and can choose whatever you want. The inner desire is to express your *etzem* as above any thing, not stuck in any one.

That is the usual order in a person's *avoda*. First he takes his nature, the way he is, and uses it for good. The next step is to learn to break out of his nature. That does not mean *iskafya* (forcing oneself), just forcing himself to act against it. It means to free himself and realize that this is not who he is: this personality that he thinks is him is just a role he is acting out, like a costume, and he can really choose to act out a different role.

You see it by Avraham having to do *gevura*, and Yaakov having to lie and cheat Esav and Lavan, because Yaakov was an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man). They had to do the opposite of their nature. ("Not sure what it was by Yitzchak really, that he had to do.") When a person does this, *davka* then he reveals his *etzem*.

sensitivity.reason: Says Yaakov Avinu had "to lie and cheat" Esav and Lavan; the point is a Torah one, but the blunt wording about a patriarch may need his approval in print.
sensitivity.publishable: You see it by Avraham having to do *gevura*, and Yaakov having to deal deceptively with Esav and Lavan, because Yaakov was an *ish tam* (a simple, wholesome man). They had to do the opposite of their nature. ("Not sure what it was by Yitzchak really, that he had to do.") When a person does this, *davka* then he reveals his *etzem*.

blocks.title: The Purim costume
blocks.text: On Purim, when you put on a costume, you feel free to do what you want, because you do not feel it reflects on you. It is a similar thing from the side of the *yechida*: a person realizes that all the *partzufim* he puts on, all the roles he plays, are like costumes he can take off.

You see it in a person like the Rebbe, who was very unpredictable: to each person, and in each situation, he would act differently, with all types of extremes, the most private and the most public, the most liberal and the most conservative. Normally these seem impossible to have together, because you see them as contradictions. The whole thing of Chassidus, when you reveal the essence, is that you realize you can have 100% of both. Whenever there is a conflict, it is not a choice of 50-50, or all of one: it is 100% of both.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זמן באה מחשבה זו לבא למעשה,
phrases.en: but when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"

phrases.he: ניכר בו התחלקות אותן אופנים שונים ממש שכבר הוחלט אצלו בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: Now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.

phrases.he: רק שמתחלה בא הרצון הזה בדרך כלל
phrases.en: first comes as a general thought,

phrases.he: שיהיה לו בנין בציור כך וכך
phrases.en: he wants this general type of a house,

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצון פרטי
phrases.en: and then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it, all the details he thinks of later.

phrases.he: לכל ענין פרטי
phrases.en: for each detail, like the kitchen, and the sink, and whatever.

phrases.he: ויורד ובא בסדר והדרגה מכלל הראשון
phrases.en: from the first general *klal*, like the *ratzon* for a house,

phrases.he: שכולל הכל בסקירה א'
לפרט רצון שהוא נקרא כלל לגבי רצונות המסתעפים ממנו
phrases.en: Then he goes from the general *ratzon* of a house to a detail of that, like the kitchen, but that's then a general thing for everything that branches off from it,

phrases.he: עד שבא אל רצון ושכל פרטי היותר אחרון
phrases.en: until it comes to the last screw,

phrases.he: שבסוף מעשה בכלות הכל כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: putting up the *mezuza* on his front door when he's finished everything.

blocks.text: **But when later he actually thinks, "Oh, I want to build a house,"** not just that he already had in him the way he would want to do it, but he actually thought about it: **now then you see everything that was already decided there with all the details.**

blocks.title: Advertising
blocks.text:
By the way, the same general idea, maybe on a little bit lower level, is advertising. The advertiser is not necessarily trying to find somebody who right now is interested in buying a car. He wants the person to set up, subconsciously, a liking, a positive association with this name. One day, when he goes to buy whatever it is, he will think of your name right away; or if he is faced with two names, he will pick yours. He was never thinking of buying it, but he set up a positive association, something he sees fits with his personality. They try to make people associate the product with being free, or being put together, whatever personality thing: they give the product a certain image, so that people who want to express themselves through that image will choose it.

The real *ratzon hamuchlat* spoken of here is that image a person wants to express himself as. The advertisers are not really setting it; they are just trying to tap into it. It is the same idea on a lower level.

All the ways he had already settled in this *ratzon hamuchlat*, his taste, now come out *l'poel* (into action), the way he actually wants to build a house in this type of a world. It **first comes as a general thought**: **he wants this general type of a house**. **And then he plans out where he wants the house to be, how he's gonna pay for it, exactly how he's gonna decorate it, all the details he thinks of later**: a particular will **for each detail, like the kitchen, and the sink, and whatever.**

It goes down in order, by levels, **from the first general klal, like the ratzon for a house**, which includes everything at one glance. **Then he goes from the general ratzon of a house to a detail of that, like the kitchen, but that's then a general thing for everything that branches off from it**, **until it comes to the last screw**: **putting up the mezuza on his front door when he's finished everything.**

That is the general idea of the ten *sefiros* of *igulim*. The first circle is the general will for the whole *dira b'tachtonim*. Then, as the *nimshal* will now say, it splits up into the will for *Atzilus* and then for *Beriya*, and each of those splits up into details for each of the ten *sefiros* of each world, down to each *prat*, even each person and each little creature that G-d made.

sections.title: The nimshal above: tehiru ila'a is the taste still within the Essence
sections.summary: Before the *tzimtzum*, in *tehiru ila'a*, G-d has the knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way, like the taste in the simple will: not yet a will for anything outside Himself, so it cannot even be called a general thought. *Tehiru tata'a*, after the *tzimtzum*, is the choice of this world: still self-knowledge, but of how something separate relates to Him, so a lower purity.

phrases.he: והנמשל מכל זה יובן למעלה בהפרש שבין בחינת טהירו עילאה ובין בחינת טהירו תתאה שלאחר הצמצום

blocks.text: The *nimshal* of all this is understood above, in the difference between *tehiru ila'a* and *tehiru tata'a* after the *tzimtzum*. *Tehiru ila'a* is like the essential simple will and what comes out from it, *Yachid* and *Kadmon*; the part of it that relates to *tehiru tata'a* is *Kadmon*. *Tehiru tata'a*, after the *tzimtzum*, is the actual revealed will.

Before the *tzimtzum* is the *etzem*, G-d's essential revelation. Included in it is G-d's knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in any way He wants, including the knowledge and ability to reveal Himself in our world. But it was included like a *hiyuli*: if He would ever choose to, in theory He would know how to do it, and He could do it. The *tzimtzum*, and the *reshimu* after it, was to actually pick which way He was going to reveal Himself. The first *ratzon kadum* is the result of the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav*: it is the actual choice, and that choice starts off as the general thought of our world.

That is the product: G-d thought of our world the way it is, the whole totality, that He is going to reveal Himself as Creator of man, with this whole thing of *galus* (exile) and *geula* (redemption) and *dira b'tachtonim*. Revealing the *etzem* is not really in this *ratzon kadum*, "I don't think," because that is higher. But the general thing of this whole *Moshiach* thing, all the way to *Moshiach*, is the first *ratzon kadum*: one particular way that G-d could reveal Himself, by making this whole *hishtalshelus*. That is *tehiru tata'a*.

phrases.he: דמה ששיער בעצמו בכח בטהירו עילאה כו'
phrases.en: that in *tehiru ila'a* it's just that Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it.

phrases.he: הוא כמו ההחלט ברצון הפשוט שבעצמות הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like a taste,

phrases.he: שעדיין לא בא כלל לבחינת התפשטות חוץ מן העצמות עדיין
phrases.en: It's not at all an actual *ratzon* for something separate from Himself.

phrases.he: וגם שיתחבר מרצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון שאחר כך,
phrases.en: even though this connects to the *hispashtus* of the *ratzon*

phrases.he: מכל מקום נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמות דאור אין סוף
phrases.en: The *ratzon muchlat* stays really hidden.

phrases.he: ועל כן למעלה הוא מבחינת כלל להיות נקרא צופה ומביט בסקירה א' כו'.
phrases.en: Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a *skira achas*.

blocks.text: What He estimated in Himself *b'koach* (in potential) means **that in tehiru ila'a it's just that Hashem has in His ability the knowledge of how to do it and the ability to do it**, **like a taste** in the simple will. **It's not at all an actual ratzon for something separate from Himself.** **Even though this connects to the hispashtus of the ratzon** that comes after, **the ratzon muchlat stays really hidden.** As was said, it is not a *makif* and a *pnimi*, so it never becomes revealed. Even the *hashara* (estimation) of *Kadmon* does not become revealed, because before the *tzimtzum* *Kadmon* includes G-d's knowledge of how to make this *hishtalshelus* and any *hishtalshelus*: just that He knows how to do particular things to reveal Himself.

**Therefore, at that stage you can't even call it a general thing, a general thought of our world that's in a skira achas** (one glance), because it is not yet a thought of something outside: it is *yedias atzmo*. It is not that with *yedias atzmo* He knows something else, as with the *ratzon kadum*; it is only *yedias atzmo*. That is why *tehiru ila'a* means it is completely pure.

*Tehiru tata'a* is the way G-d looks at the world as an expression of Himself. It is still called *yedias atzmo*, but a *yedias atzmo* in which there is a *nivra* (a created being). So it is not completely pure: it is a lower purity, because it is still a self-revelation, but of what you are going to get out of something separate, how something separate relates to you.

So you are still thinking of yourself. As will be said, the real thing of the *ratzon kadum* is still not a will for a house; it is a will for a home. At the *ratzon kadum* you really want the feeling you are going to get from it. The actual thought, when you start to picture a physical house according to your society, will be explained later: that really happens in *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.title: The clingy baby
blocks.text: At a certain age a person gets a desire to be independent, to settle down, and that is always included in a person's nature: a person without a house is not a person. It is essential to his desires. In the *ratzon hamuchlat* you know it about even a little baby. He is a clingy baby who does not want to let go of his mother for a second, and you say, "Right now you don't want to, but I'm telling you, one day he's going to want to get out of here and have his own house and only come back and visit every now and then." "How do you know?" "Well, I know the nature of people." Now the kid does not even know it, and he would not believe you if you told him.

When it first comes out, it does not come out as a will to go buy an apartment or a house. It first comes out as an uneasiness: the person feels unsettled, feels that he needs to look for something, and starts looking for what will fit that. Then he visits somebody who has his own place, feels it gives a certain feeling of independence, and realizes that was what he was looking for: that uneasy feeling was really a will for that.

The point is that the *ratzon kadum* is already a will for a particular *taanug* (delight) to be fulfilled in the outside world, to express yourself outside in a certain way; you are just looking for what will do that. That is why the *igulim* are said to be like the soul: it is not yet enclothed in the actual tangible thing of the world.

sections.title: The second will: the Kav and its first circle, the ratzon kadum
sections.summary: After the *tzimtzum*, the simple will comes to spread forth: that is the *hiyuli Kav*, a general system of priorities. Its first product is the ultimate goal, the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, which includes every particular will and is called *ratzon kadum*: everything after it is only a means to it.

phrases.he: אך הרצון הב' הוא אחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
שעולה רצון הפשוט המוחלט שבעצמות לבא לידי בחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: that something from this *ratzon pashut* came to actually do it, that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.

phrases.he: הוא בחינת הקו וחוט ההיולי שכולל כל המשכות פרטיות שבו מראשו לסופו כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: The second will is after the *tzimtzum*: the simple, absolute will in the Essence rises to spread forth, meaning **that something from this ratzon pashut came to actually do it, that Hashem decided, picked what He's going to actually do.** That is the *hiyuli Kav*, which includes all the particular drawings-down from its beginning to its end.

This is the general idea of the *Kav*. The *reshimu*, with the head of the *Kav*, is the general goal, and the *Kav* is the general way, the ability to figure out how you are going to accomplish the goal: you create a general system of priorities, so that when you put the two together you will know how to react in any situation. The first result of this is that you create your ultimate goal for yourself, the *ratzon kadum*. That is the first creation that comes out from your *reshimu* and your *Kav*: they make this first will for yourself.

phrases.he: ובחינת מקיף הראשון שבו הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה,
שזהו כמשל רצון הכללי לבנין גדול כולל כל מה שבפרטיו מראשו לסופו בבת א'
ואחר כך מתחלק בו בסדר והדרגה מכלל לפרט
phrases.en: Then this gets split up,

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like in the *mashal* we said about the house.

blocks.text: Its first *makif* is called *tehiru tata'a*, like the general will for a great building that includes all its details from beginning to end. In a person's whole life, this is like the general desire for fulfillment, or self-expression, or something like that. **Then this gets split up**: this is your top priority, your original goal.

This is like the *etzem* of the *yechida*, the *Moshiach* within each person. A person who finds it is redeemed: he has found the *geula*, he is fulfilled, he has arrived, "whatever you want to call it." Then it splits up into the lesser priorities, and you make a whole hierarchy according to your *Kav*, finding more and more details until you figure out what you want in day-to-day life, **like in the mashal we said about the house.**

phrases.he: והיינו כמו כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט ההיולי לבא לגלוי דוקא, היה כולל כל פרטי הרצונות
phrases.en: And this is the *inyan* that when he had a particular *ratzon*, it came out, he already had all the things that he wants to do included in that.

phrases.he: והוא הרצון הכולל כולם,
phrases.en: and this first *ratzon* that comes out *b'gilui* includes them all,

phrases.he: ונקרא רצון קדום לכל מה שבא אחריו
phrases.en: This is called the original *ratzon* for everything that comes after.

blocks.text: When it rose in His simple, *hiyuli* will to come *davka* into revelation, it included all the particular wills. **When he had a particular ratzon, it came out, he already had all the things that he wants to do included in that.** **And this first ratzon that comes out b'gilui includes them all.** **This is called the original ratzon for everything that comes after**, the *ratzon kadum*: original, meaning that everything else is only its details, just a means of accomplishing this goal.

That is the difference between *kadum* and *rishon*, spoken of once before. *Rishon* (first) means only that it comes first, in any order; *kadum* means that the only meaning of the things after it is to fulfill it.

For example, the will for money is not an essential will. It is a will to fulfill a deeper will: being able to buy what you need, or having possessions, which can relate to doing what you want without worrying, or to stature, people considering you successful, all different things. But if you trace all the wills back, you come to one essential desire, the inner goal.

sections.title: Down to the last detail, all included in the first circle around all four worlds
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum* come the particular wills: for *Atzilus* with its ten *sefiros*, still hidden until it is revealed, then to create *Beriya*, down to the last will of *Asiya*. All of them are included in the first circle, the beginning of the *Kav*, which surrounds the four worlds equally because they are all equally only a means to its goal. That they can be cut off from it is the root of *Tohu*.

phrases.he: ואחר כך בא רצון זה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: And then the details are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו הרצון להאציל
phrases.en: like the desire for *Atzilus*,

phrases.he: ובו כלול עשר ספירות בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: and this includes ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: ועדיין הכל בהעלם
phrases.en: but you didn't actually do *Atzilus* yet.

phrases.he: עד שבא לידי גלוי שהוא כשנאצל האור בבחינת האצילות כו'
phrases.en: then it comes *b'gilui*: that's when he actually was *ne'etzal*.

blocks.text: **And then the details are revealed, like the desire for Atzilus.** In the *mashal* of the house spoken of before, the guy wanted to build a house after he got married and went to the architect. The will for *Atzilus* is to figure out what you want. It is like sitting down with the architect, and he asks you, "What are you looking for?" You are not talking about a house; you are talking about yourself, what you like. **And this includes ten sefiros** with all their details.

blocks.title: Out to dinner, and the door
blocks.text: **But you didn't actually do Atzilus yet**: it is all hidden. It is like when people say, "What are you going to do tonight?" "Oh, let's go out for dinner." "Okay." You drive over there, you get to the door, and you say, "Oh, where are we going to get the *ratzon* to open the door?" "Well, that was included in the *ratzon* to go to the restaurant." All the later wills that you know will have to happen are included in the original desire.

blocks.title: Shall we drive to the real estate agent?
blocks.text: Like a guy who wants a house: he did not actually think of it yet, but when it comes up you ask him, "Do you want a kitchen?" "Yeah, of course I want a kitchen." "Well, so are we going to drive to the real estate agent?" "Oh yeah, sure, we'll drive to the real estate agent." He did not think about the details, but it is understood that whatever will have to be done for this, he wants to do.

So the way they are included in *tehiru tata'a* is not in actuality. It is just a general thought, the first general will that includes all the later ones. When they come up in actuality, those are the later circles, the *igulim* of *Atzilus* and of *Beriya*: that is when it splits up into each thing. They cannot relate to a specific manifestation in a physical, limited world until you pick a form, really a *kli*, and that is more like *tehiru tata'a*.

There is a *yechida* with a name and a *yechida* without a name. The *yechida* with a name is the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*: the *igulim* and *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, when you actually make a picture of your essence. The real essence, the *yechida* without a name, is like before the *tzimtzum*. That *Yachid* is the real essence, but included in your essence is that you can have a thing like *chesed* and *Malchus*. *Chesed* is like *Echad* and *Malchus* is like *Kadmon*, which is why he highlights those two wills.

There is the ability to pick a general, abstract desire, to transcend the form and make a general thing that includes everything; and there is the ability to pick a particular *kli* to express that abstract, transcendent thing, which is like *Kadmon*, or *Malchus*. In the *etzem* those two abilities, like *chesed* and *gevura*, are just a *yecholes* (an ability), not really three levels in actuality. It is just understood that the *etzem* is the *etzem*, and therefore it can do both *chesed* and *gevura*, but they are not divided out yet. The *tzimtzum* is when you choose which *Echad* and *Kadmon* you want, and the result of the *tzimtzum* is *tehiru tata'a*.

But at that point you do not yet know that it is a house, a building. You just know that you want to express a certain *inyan* of yourself, how you want to express yourself, and then you have to look for what will express it. If you want to express a certain *taanug* of a feeling of independence, you go looking, and you find the desire for a house to match it.

That will be spoken of later: it is the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, when you make your world view and your self-image. When you normally say an *etzem*, or a person, you mean it as already limited to being a person, already with only ten *sefiros*; all those limitations really start in the *ratzon kadum* of *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* is the first time it is like a person.

That came from the *tzimtzum*, and the chain in the person happens at the same time as the chain in the worlds: G-d had this *ratzon kadum*, which made the soul of a certain form, and then He made the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, which made the way the soul will go into the body, the general mission of the soul.

The *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon* is like *Moshiach*, the form of *Moshiach* as a person; the *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon* are like the *dira b'tachtonim*, its *pnimiyus*. The *nekuda*, the *ratzon kadum*, is the *dira b'tachtonim*, and the way it is expressed in our world is all the things the *halacha* and the *Midrashim* say about how it is actually going to be physically by *Moshiach*.

And after that, **then it comes b'gilui: that's when he actually was ne'etzal** (emanated). *Atzilus* is the revelation of the ten *sefiros* of *igulim* of *Atzilus* that were included in the original thing.

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא
phrases.en: the next *ratzon* is the *ratzon* to create,

phrases.he: יש מאין כו'
ובו שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and then it also has ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: עד הרצון היותר אחרון
phrases.en: so the final most *ratzon*,

phrases.he: שהוא כל אשר חפץ עשה כו', סוף הכל

blocks.text: Then it comes out in revelation: **the next ratzon is the ratzon to create**. That is like when you figure out what will fulfill your desires. If there is a desire to swim, we will make a swimming pool; if a desire for *farbrengens*, we will make a nice dining room with room, and a floor that is not carpet, so you can clean up messes. That is like *Beriya*. Not the actual *Beriya*: the desire to do it. The desire to do it, the general abstract wills for how you want it done, are the *igulim* of *Beriya*. The will to create *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing), with *sechel* and *middos*: **and then it also has ten sefiros.**

Down to **the final most ratzon**, "all that He desired, He did": in the will for a house, putting up the *mezuza*, moving in all the furniture, the last fine touches; in the world, all the little details of everyday life in the physical world, like the weather today. That is *Asiya* in action, the end of everything.

phrases.he: וכל פרטים הללו נכללו ברצון הקדום
phrases.en: all these details, they were all included in the original desire

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת השפעה על כל פנים אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: which is already an actual *hashpaa*, an actual thing that relates to the outside world, and after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ראשית הקו כו',
phrases.en: and this first circle is considered the beginning of the *Kav*, it's the first *gilui* of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: והיינו עיגול הראשון שאחר המשכת ראשית הקו ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: this is the first circle after the *hiyuli Kav*,

blocks.text: **All these details, they were all included in the original desire**, **which is already an actual hashpaa** (influence), **an actual thing that relates to the outside world, and after the tzimtzum.** **And this first circle is considered the beginning of the Kav, it's the first gilui of the Kav.** *Reshis hakav* can mean the *hiyuli Kav*, or it can mean this first circle, the first revelation of the *Kav*. Along the *Kav*, it is the top priority.

Practically, this is what it says in *HaYom Yom*: every single detail of creation, even the way a blade of grass sways in the wind, is not only by *hashgacha pratis* (individual Divine providence), but is necessary for the entire *kavana* (intent) of creation.

blocks.title: The leaves in this corner
blocks.text: When G-d said, "I want a *dira b'tachtonim*," you ask Him, "Well, do You want the leaves on the tree in this and this corner to blow back and forth 300,267,371 times?" And Hashem says, "Of course. How else could I have a *dira b'tachtonim* if it wasn't just like that?"

Every single *prat* is there for some reason we do not appreciate right now, but will, throughout the seventh millennium. The whole reason all the details of creation exist is as a tool to fulfill this will; each one fulfills a certain detail of that will, or else it would not exist. That is the inner motivation that creates them. **This is the first circle after the hiyuli Kav.**

phrases.he: שנקרא מקיף כללי לכללות כל הד' עולמות דאבי''ע,
phrases.en: this first *ratzon* is called the general *makif* for all the four worlds of *ABYA*,

phrases.he: שמקיף אותם בשוה
phrases.en: that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.

phrases.he: שנקרא מחשבה כללית שצופה ומביט בסקירה א' מראש לסוף הכל כו'
phrases.en: it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.

blocks.text: **This first ratzon is called the general makif for all the four worlds of ABYA**, **that it surrounds them all equally, meaning that they're all equally just a means to accomplish this goal.** The order they come out in is set by the *Kav*, but it does not essentially have to be that way: without the *Kav* there is no chain in the *igulim*. From the side of the wills there is no real chain: each one comes directly from the *ratzon hamuchlat*, and the *Kav* just decides what the priority should be. That is why a person's wills can jump out of place.

blocks.title: The son who forgot his mother
blocks.text: There are stories of somebody from a very poor family whose dream was that one day he would be able to support his poor mother and give her a better life. He goes out to work and makes a lot of money, then gets caught up in the desire for money and forgets about his mother. He will not give her money; he might not even give to himself, he might become a miser. People can lose their will like that. Or people who get all into business and forget about their families: the whole reason they were working was to have the means to do the things they really enjoy, *Torah* and *mitzvos* and their family, the people who are important to them.

How does a person forget? It is the thing of *Tohu*. Since each will has the *etzem* in it, you can get totally locked into it: you feel the *taanug* in it, the self-expression, and you forget the need for anything else. You can get totally absorbed in any will without connecting it to anything, and it does not have to be a means to an end. A means to an end is *tikun* (rectification). But that too is part of the *bechira*.

That is why *Tohu* is so powerful: it takes a certain maturity to appreciate that there is a deeper *taanug* in having it this way, with the priorities and everything. *Tohu* and *tikun* will be spoken of later: the *igulim* and *yosher* are the root of *Tohu* and *tikun*.

This first circle is called a general thought: **it's called a general thought that it sees everything in one glance.**

phrases.he: וזהו ביאור ענין כללי לכללות ענין הקו הזה
phrases.en: this is the general idea of the *Kav*,

phrases.he: ופרטי אופניו במה שמתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: and the details of how it circles and circles again,

phrases.he: יובן לפי אופן משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: now we can understand the general idea of what we mean by concentric circles by this *mashal*.

phrases.he: וכמו שיתבאר בסמוך בעזרת ה׳ ודי למבין:
phrases.en: and now we'll explain more about it in the next chapter

blocks.text: **This is the general idea of the Kav**: it starts off as a general thing, then measures out the details and sets everything up like that. **And the details of how it circles and circles again**: **now we can understand the general idea of what we mean by concentric circles by this mashal.** **And now we'll explain more about it in the next chapter**: how it goes circle inside of circle, and how in *yosher* it is the opposite. "Well, we'll see in the next chapter."

reviewQuestions.question: What are the *igulim* and the *yosher* of the *Kav*, and what do the water in the carved troughs and the soul before and in the body show about them?
Why is the first circle, *tehiru tata'a*, compared to a teacher's ultimate goal, and what does the story of Rabbi Chodakov and the *shliach* teach about it?
How is the *ratzon hamuchlat* like an artist's style, and why does it have no general and particular?
What makes a will *murkav*, and how does the will for a house show it?
Why is *tehiru tata'a* a lower purity than *tehiru ila'a*, though both are G-d's self-knowledge?
Why does the first circle surround the four worlds equally, and how can a person's wills "jump out of place"?
